title: A new way to think about a repo
what: Not a pile of files and commits: living lines, each with its own author and history, that close back up as plain git whenever you like.

title: Multiplayer, every which way
what: Human to human, human to AI, AI to AI: everyone in the same repo at once, live, line by line, and every line says who.

title: Own your git history
what: Every line, author and rev is yours, in a real git repo you can clone anywhere. Nobody upstream gets a say.

title: Edit live, together
what: Lines have stable ids, so agents editing different lines never collide. Edits stream to every open page.

title: Private lines in a public repo
what: Hide some lines from everyone but the crew: on the page, in blame, in shares, and blank in git.

title: Share some lines, not the repo
what: A live link to a range that follows those lines as the file changes, even from a private repo.

title: Public or private repos
what: A private repo you can't see answers 404, in search too.

title: Time travel
what: Replay a file to any edit it ever had, with blame per line.

title: Cut
what: Some lines plus everything they use, as their own branch: run the tests, then merge the fix back.

title: The dependency doctor
what: Proposes safe updates on a branch, tests them in a throwaway clone, and can have an agent fix what broke.

title: Runs on a laptop too
what: The same app runs as a desktop binary, with sqlite standing in for D1 and git on disk standing in for Artifacts.

title: A file is a Durable Object
what: Each file has one writer, so every edit from every person and agent lands in one order.

title: See who's here
what: Presence shows who else has the file open, as they type.

title: Every line knows who wrote it
what: Author and time on every line, people and agents alike.

title: Branches and merges, by line
what: A three-way merge by line id: moved blocks keep their edits, and real conflicts are named one stretch at a time.

title: Build changes get a second look
what: A branch that touches package.json, lockfiles or deploy config waits for “I've read the build changes”.

title: Closes up as a real git commit
what: Cataloguing pushes a real commit to Cloudflare Artifacts, built by hand: no git library.

title: Clone it with plain git
what: Every repo has a git clone line with a read token that lasts an hour.

title: Levels
what: Small, well-loved repos (mitt, clsx, Ky, Zustand, Hono, Express, Preact) to browse and fork.

title: Dig up any GitHub repo
what: Paste a URL, a remote or a gh repo clone line and fork it into a git repo you own. Upstream never hears about it.

title: Share cards for X
what: A cut's code and its test result, drawn into a PNG inside the Worker with no image library.

title: Put a coding agent on a file
what: claude, codex, pi or opencode edit a file, and their lines land live, blamed on the agent.

title: Rusty Buns fit
what: Every repo page says how easily it ships as a desktop binary, a Worker and a server.

title: Deploy for real
what: Ship the repo's stack to a stage you pick. Only a person ships; agents never start a deploy.

title: Webhooks for CI/CD
what: GitHub-shaped JSON, signed with HMAC-SHA256, logged, and retried when it fails.

title: One command palette, one API
what: Press ⌘K. Every action is one API call, shown next to it, so people and agents do the same things the same way.

title: Search code
what: Full-text search over everything committed that you're allowed to see.

title: Playlists of code
what: Collect line ranges you love from any file you can see. Each track follows its lines as they change.

title: Your profile is your own HTML
what: Write your own HTML and CSS, sandboxed, no scripts.

title: Sign in your way
what: GitHub, Google, or email and password, and a handle that's yours for good.

title: Rate limits that queue
what: Over the cap, a dig waits its turn in line instead of failing, and finds you on your profile when it's done.
